title: SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD
status_notes: Final version 7.0 of 11/08/2017 (cover and change log, pp. 1 and 6); verified 2017-08-18 and approved 2017-08-22 by digital signature (p. 2). It is the newest ICD issue in the library. The source site files it as the MOC-applicable MIB ICD for Solar Orbiter (source URL). Later issues are not stated in the document; the wiki's MIB schema (tools/pyscos2000_schema_icd72.json) follows ICD 7.2, which is not in the library.
summary:
Version 7.0 (August 2017) of ESOC's SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD (EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001), the reference definition of the SCOS-2000 Mission Information Base (MIB) as tab-separated ASCII tables. This copy was published on the Solar Orbiter instrument-team site as the MIB ICD applicable to the Solar Orbiter MOC, so it is the closest available specification for reading the public Solar Orbiter MIB.

Chapter 2 sets the rules: Unix-format files with one table per `<table>.dat`, tab separators with every field present, synthetic parameter expression files, per-domain databases, import checks with their fallback values, and the R5 handling of sequences and displays as XML in the FARC. Chapter 3 maps database items to tables, summarises the 51 tables and defines every field with type, length, key and mandatory/default markers. It covers monitoring parameters (PCF with 23 fields), synthetic parameters, user-defined constants, dynamic configuration variables, system-control parameters, the calibrations (cur, caf/cap, txf/txp, mcf, lgf), limit checks (ocf/ocp), packet identification and decoding (pid, pic, tpcf, plf, vpd), groups and displays, and on the commanding side TC headers, commands (ccf, dst, cpc, cdf, ptv), sequences, verification, parameter sets, de-calibrations and range checks.

Appendix A lists every supported PTC/PFC pair, including Unix time (9,30), and the raw value formats. Appendix B shows the table relationships, and Appendix C describes PUS support and limitations per service. Annex 1 repeats the change history, and the new Annex 2 lists the 7.0 changes by S2K ticket. Among them: Unix file format, reserved ground-station parameter names, PIC_APID as a key, maximum TC parameter sizes, the TC(11,4) time-tag wrapper, and future CPC_ENDIAN and VPD_FIXREP=-1 extensions.

key_points.text: RD-1 is now CG-0003 'SCOS-2000 Configuration Variables' and RD-15 is EGOS-EUD-S2K-SUM-1001 'EUD4S2K Software User Manual'.
The ASCII files are in Unix format (S2K-7551); the example off-line database is now only MS ACCESS, the ORACLE reference having been removed (S2K-8137).
Each record must contain every field, at least as a separator; null fields contain only the tab character.
Section 3.2 summarises 51 ASCII tables, from vdf to prv, including cur, lgf, grp, grpa, grpk and the optional dst routing table.

PCF_NAME (Char(8)) may not start with 'VAR', 'GVAR' or '$', and the names NNOiiii, CEBiiii, KRUiiii, MSPiiii, VL2iiii, PERiiii, REDiiii and MLGiiii (iiii = 0000-9999) are reserved for ground-station telemetry.
The PCF table has 23 fields (PCF_NAME ... PCF_ENDIAN); PCF_DESCR is Char(24) and PCF_CURTX Char(10).

System Control parameters: the SCTL application stores the status of monitored SCOS-2000 server families as TM packets, and SCTLgenerateMIB generates the corresponding MIB entries before SCTL first runs.
The PID table has 16 fields; PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_PI2_VAL and PID_SPID are marked as key fields, and PID_APID is Number(5).

The maximum command size comes from MISC variable CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (default 248 bytes), reduced by the header (sum of PCDF_LEN), the CRC (CMD_CRC_SIZE, default 2 bytes) and, for time-tagged commands, the TC(11,4) wrapper (CMD_LOAD_TT_NAME, default 20 bytes).

Commands can be destined to the spacecraft or to other control domains such as ground equipment; throw-event commands (from R5.0) are encoded per [RD-18] for SLE and [RD-19] for NIS throw events and cannot be blocked with other entries.
The CCF table has 21 fields, the last being CCF_SUBSCHED (Number(5)).
CPC has 16 fields; CPC_CORR and CPC_OBTID support time-correlated encoding of time parameters, and CPC_ENDIAN (default 'B') is a future extension (S2K-7749).
CVS has 7 fields; the optional CVS_UNCERTAINTY gives a stage-specific verification window that overrides the default in the TM Spacon.
Absolute time PTC=9 PFC=30 (Unix format, 8 octets: 4 bytes of seconds since 1 January 1970 followed by 4 bytes of microseconds) is supported although it is not defined in the PUS.

Appendix C: SCOS-2000 encodes and decodes all PUS packet types within the data-type limits, and describes service-specific processing such as service 1 report-based verification and the service 11 ground image of the on-board schedule.

Annex 2 lists the 7.0 changes with the applicable SCOS releases, e.g. S2K-8073 (maximum TC parameter sizes, 5.5.3/6.0.0 or higher), S2K-8528 (PIC_APID part of the key, 4.2 or higher) and S2K-8226 (TC(11,4) encoding according to CDF, 5.5.4 and higher).
S2K-6884 lists reserved parameter names, S2K-8572 and S2K-8778 forbid PCF_CORR/CPC_CORR='Y' for relative-time parameters, and S2K-7750 adds the future VPD_FIXREP value '-1'.

notes: Source: solarorbiter.irap.omp.eu, the file 'MOC-applicable MIB egos-mcs-s2k-icd-0001-version7.0-FINAL.pdf'. Printed page 1 is PDF page 15 (offset +14); every page carries a 2017 ESA copyright footer. Broken cross-reference '(see Section f below)' on p. 18. Both PURPOSE and SCOPE are numbered 1.1. The page numbers given in the section 3.2 summary ('See page ...') do not match this issue's pagination. Section 3.3.3.2.1 (ccf) writes '[RD-18}' with a mismatched bracket. The digital-signature block on p. 2 includes an e-mail address, not reproduced here. Appendix C cites PUS sections via [AD-2]/[AD-5], as in earlier 6.x issues. Related library items: icd-6-9-archive-org (predecessor), icd-6-7-drafta, icd-5-1-tos-gci; the Solar Orbiter MIB releases mib-20250916m25925pfms001-sol and mib-20200416m10720pfms001-sol; RD-20 corresponds to ecss-e-70-41a-30jan2003-pus; RD-8 is an older issue of ccsds-301-0-301x0b4e1. Section 3.3.2.1.5 lists the SCTL-generated tables as 'PLF, PID, TPCF, OCF, OCP, TXT, TXP', where TXT presumably means TXF.
